why: Deep dive 31 Oct: PP+Vox ≥176 in all 20 recent polls (avg 197), ~90%. YES then needs a PP–Vox deal and a passed investiture by ~29 Jan, 37 days after the Cortes meet on 23 Dec, over Christmas. Only 2019 (35 days) was that fast without a single-party majority; PP–Vox regional deals took 46–122 days (3 of 8 within 63). Caretaker status doesn't count. ~0.52 YES vs market 0.68.

Deep dive 31 Oct: 15 Jan is 23 days after the Cortes meet (23 Dec) with Christmas and Epiphany in between. Only single-party governments (2000-2011) were invested that fast; PP needs Vox's yes votes and Vox has joined every regional government it backed. ~0.30 YES vs market 0.62.

Deep dive 31 Oct: an investiture by 31 Dec needs a 2011-style 7-day process over Christmas (~3%). The bigger risk is resolution: this market lacks the caretaker clause, and the BOE decree 'declaring the cese' of Sánchez (as RD 694/2023 did two days after the 2023 vote) could be argued as YES. Smart money is heavily on NO.

Deep dive 31 Oct: YES needs three more failed PM votes and the Speaker formally setting a date by 31 Dec (Vallagen 1:3); the government route is closed (caretaker since 17 Sep, and no government may order one before ~28 Dec). Norlén says he'll be 'lite varsam' with vote 3, and in 2018 he refused a pre-Christmas vote. Seats 176 red-green v 173 Tidö. ~10% YES vs market 19.5%.
